**MOD-φ CONVERGENCE, I: NORMALITY ZONES AND PRECISE DEVIATIONS**

*VALENTIN FÉRAY, PIERRE-LOÏC MÉLIOT, AND ASHKAN NIKEGHBALI*

103 pp, 55 sections.

**Abstract.** In this paper, we use the framework of mod-φ convergence to prove pre- cise large or moderate deviations for quite general sequences of real valued random variables (Xn)n∈N, which can be lattice or non-lattice distributed. We establish precise estimates of the ﬂuctuations P[Xn ∈tnB], instead of the usual estimates for the rate of exponential decay log(P[Xn ∈tnB]). Our approach provides us with a systematic way to characterise the normality zone, that is the zone in which the Gaussian approxima- tion for the tails is still valid. Besides, the residue function measures the extent to which this approximation fails to hold at the edge of the normality zone. The ﬁrst sections of the article are devoted to a proof of these abstract results and comparisons with existing results.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 1.2 Theoretical results; 1.3 Applications; 1.4 Forthcoming works; 1.5 Discussion on our hypotheses; Acknowledgements; 2 Preliminaries; 2.1 Basic examples of mod-convergence; 2.2 Legendre-Fenchel transforms; 2.3 Gaussian integrals; 3 Fluctuations in the case of lattice distribu; 3.1 Lattice and non-lattice distributions; 3.2 Deviations at the scale O(tn); 3.3 Central limit theorem at the scales o(tn) ; 4 Fluctuations in the non-lattice case; 4.1 Berry-Esseen estimates; 4.2 Deviations at scale O(tn)
